channel.title: No man's an island
channel.description: Posts in the discussion thread "No man's an island" - Here's the first draft of my first SCP article, up for review.

item.title: Re: No man's an island
item.content:encoded:
[+] Overall
[-] Overall

I don't really like this as a whole; or, rather, I like what it's trying to be more than I like what it is. As written, the story is too static: too much of -2's growth is elided or not able to be shown, and so it just feels…not very interesting.

Like, consider: the way the reader learns that -2 has learnt that he's the source of his power, not the toys, is from -2 just…saying it? There's no like, process of -2 learning this or trying to figure out how it works; and so it feels underwhelming: it's not like, a triumphant, climactic moment of character growth because like, there's no struggle to get there, or even anything we're shown that gradually leads that way. It doesn't really land from just being interesting either because the description explicitly tells us this is the case.

Equally, his growth as a person is elided: we see him being really sad in the tests but there's no real escalation for the sadness or anything, and because the tests are so detached from -2's emotional state, we don't really emphasise with him, so -2 doesn't feel like it's him reaching a breaking point so much as it feels like just a random point. But moving on from there, we don't see any of his recovery, or his struggle to become less suicidal or any of that growth, so it doesn't really land right.

And since neither of these things land properly, the whole thing just feels…passive and uninteresting. It feels almost like we're getting a slice of life story except without any of the charm you can pack into one, and so I'm just…left feeling underwhelmed by this as a whole.

If I was to be extremely, brutally honest: I don't think this can really work as a SCP. The core of the story is too focussed on -2 and his growth and evolution as a person for the detached, cold format forced by a SCP file to effectively tell his story. If this was a tale, from the perspective of -2, you'd be able to convey his despair a lot better, and how the testing ruins his mental health, and how he gradually gets better once they employ a psychologist; but since you can't really…show any of that, it'll likely never land.

[-] Overall
[+] Line By Line
[-] Line By Line

Gonna note that I can miss stuff; flag things which are right as being wrong and indeed flag things which are deliberately wrong.
I'll likely use strikethrough to indicate stuff to remove and green text to indicate stuff to add.

and tests on its protective abilities are to be conducted monthly.
Every two months.

I would make the 'every two months' be more clearly something that was edited into the sentence for a time perhaps; though, there's likely not an easy way to do that: perhaps "and tests on its protective abilities are to be conducted monthly every two months." would be the best way

No more tests are to be conducted on SCP-XXXX without Dr Morter's approval and SCP-XXXX-2 is to have weekly meetings with Dr. Young from the Psychology and parapsychology departementdepartment.

This should be two sentences; the before/after around the first "and" are too separate for this to flow nicely together, and it feels like the first part would fit more neatly in the previous paragraph.

I'm also generally pretty against putting in specific people in ConProcs as opposed to roles (e.g. I'd use 'without approval from the Site Director' instead of 'without Dr Morter's approval') largely because what happens if Morter is e.g. killed or retires or w/e.

Psychological help should also be provided to SCP-XXXX-2 on demand.

I'm not necessarily sure about 'on demand' here; it feels a little vague and a little ripe for abuse and I kinda feel like the previous sentence covers this concept well enough.

SCP-XXXX-1 consists of 5 stuffed animals, belonging to SCP-XXXX-2, designated SCP-XXXX-1-A to SCP-XXXX-1-E.

You open the description referring to -1, which doesn't feature in the ConProcs, and also never describe a base SCP-XXXX thing during the description: it feels like the designation changed mid drafting and the rest of the article needs updating to take this into account.

IMO: whatever the first sentence of your description describes should be the base anomaly which the story is centred upon; in this case the humanoid. It should also be the hook: you want to hint at something interesting to make a reader go 'yes, I want to know more about this'.

SCP-XXXX-2 is a Caucasian Canadian adult male presenting severe signs of depression.

does -2 come from Canada or Caucasus? if you mean the male is white, say 'white Canadian' instead.

SCP-XXXX-2's anomaly manifests when it faces a situation of fear or distress before coming in contact withwhile not in the presence of at least one SCP-XXXX-1 entityinstance.

The current phrasing felt vague about the relation between the fear and the -1 instance and anomalous effects activating: specifically in that it implies that there's a period between 'exposed to fear' and 'activation of anomalous effects' where the bear could be applied whilst also being vague about how long that is. The change of entity to instance is cos 'entity' implies something alive, and not like, a regular teddy bear.

I don't like the start: 'anomaly manifests' feels needlessly vague about what happens here and I would prefer something like: "SCP-XXXX-2 manifests a protective sphere" as an opening here.

While the sphere is present, nothing is able to enter nor exit the sphere, with the exception of other SCP-XXXX-1 objects

The earlier phrasing implies -1 can't be present for the sphere to form; so the 'other' feels iffy here.

looses contact with every SCP-XXXX-1 entities.

same for this; the phrasing of the activation implies the sphere only occurs when there's no contact.

SCP-XXXX-2 also has a behavior of coming in contact with the most SCP-XXXX-1 possible during these events, even though this has no real effect on its abilities.

'this has no real effect on its abilities' feels super unclinical and I just, generally don't like this sentence as a whole?

Per 12/21/2020, SCP-XXXX-2 has accepted its anomalous property as its own, but still needs SCP-XXXX-1 objects to activate it.

This should really refer to an incident that happened rather than a date; or at least be 'After 12/21/2020,….'

He was apprehended by psychological staff, before being taken to site 43.

'psychological staff' feels iffy here cos it doesn't really seem like they should be doing this. Also site designations are always in the format of 'Site-43', with the capital and the hyphen.

The following interview was conducted by Dr Morter, assigned as lead researcher for SCP-XXXX, upon SCP-XXXX's arrival at the site:

You're missing an empty line between the previous paragraph and this one.

Do you know why you find yourself here?

This feels like a really weird question to ask because I'm struggling to see a situation where the answer isn't 'no'?

You are in the SCP Foundation, we will be containing and doing tests on you because you manifest an anomaly, which could be a danger for other people and yourself if aknowledged by too many outside of our organisation.

'acknowledged' is the correct spelling but there's something about this whole spiel that feels…really iffy and I'm not sure what. It flows weirdly, I think, but I'm not sure why.

Do you mean my animals' protection?

It feels odd, to me, for someone to refer to their stuffed toys as "my animals'"

Dr Morter is seen writing down some notes.

I'd cut this; we can assume that he is taking down notes where relevant and this doesn't like…add to the knowledge we've seen in any way? Like, it doesn't characterise Morter more or indicate he's realised something or anything, so it just feels…extraneous?

Also, by our Ethics Comitee's new recommandationsdue to the Ethics Committee's new recommendations concerning human SCPs I must ask you if you had someone you wanted to talk to one last time, before they get amnesticized and forget about you.

This feels like a really bad recommendation for the EC to make

Almost inaudibly. Its head is now lowered, facing the ground.

This flows weirdly: I would describe it's posture first and then say almost inaudibly; but I'd also probably use more words to describe it maybe? I'm not sure.

Louder, but the sound is muffled by SCP-XXXX-2's arms, which'swhich it's head is now between, laid on the table.

Something about this feels kinda iffy but I can't quite place why.

Until guards arrived in the interrogation room, SCP-XXXX-2 stayed in the same position for 3 minutes

Why did it take the guards three minutes to arrive at the room? It feels like there should be guards literally outside the door in case of emergency.

SCP-XXXX-2 seems to believe the sphere does not come from him, but SCP-XXXX-1-A to -E

The description and the interview already covered all this, so we don't like, actually need this whole section.

the agent shoots on the sphere in a way that could not hurt SCP-XXXX-2.

simply stopped is course when touchingit touched the sphere, seemingly loosing all of its speed upon contact with it.

We don't need to be told it lost all it's speed upon contact cos 'stopped when it touched the sphere' conveys that.

Analysis

This section (up to the italics) conveys no new information and could be cut.

SCP-XXXX-2 tried putting it downout without taking any SCP-XXXX-1 in his hands,

'without picking up an SCP-XXXX-1 instance' would be less janky than 'without taking any SCP-XXXX-1 in his hands'

until it started spreading around him. He then ran and sat in the only untouched corner

This doesn't create a clear picture of the fire: 'spreading around him' implies 'encircled' to me, so there being an 'untouched corner' feels, weird?

with SCP-XXXX-1 objects in his arms while hyperventilating, the sphere appearing the instant he touched SCP-XXXX-1-C.

I… don't really like how this is phrased. There's a clear image of him unmoving, slumped in a corner, with toys in his arms; and the idea of the sphere appearing when he touches -1-C feels weird because like….he's already touching them all?

The moment the fire touched the sphere, it evaporated into water vapour

'evaporation' is a specific thing in chemistry and I'm not sure fire can do that?

It's the third test and it still went horribly after the procedure ended.

'went horribly after the procedure ended' feels…iffy? It feels too much like you're telling us about bad things instead of showing us them.

regarding SCP-XXXX-2 are to be stopped until Dr. Morter approves of itthem.

'reapproves' might be better than 'approves' too

+ Addendum XXXX.C : Incident report : Incident XXXX-2.1

This is a janky ass title; I feel like you need to settle on giving this either an incident title or an addendum title instead of doing both.

I'd also shove this into a quoteblock too.

SCP-XXXX-2 is seen bashing his head against the wall of his cell while holding SCP-XXXX-1 objects, seemingly attempting to [EXPUNGED].

Why is this expunged? It's pretty clear that this is a suicide attempt from context; and so the data being hidden to the person reading the file feels weird as a baseline. But expungement is a step further: this data has been destroyed. It no longer exists, not even in the highest clearance version of this file. So it doesn't really like, make sense in universe and it doesn't really do anything out of universe other than blunten the impact of what you're saying so I'd just…use the word.

I'm concussioned.

'concussed'

I will answer to your question today, because I'm so done with you people that I don't even care about what you will do to me next. How good could I [EXPUNGED] be?

You're allowed to swear in a SCP article.

a [EXPUNGED] looserloser that saw talked to nobody.

Looks like my situation hasn't changed huh?

45 seconds of silence take place between the SCP and the doctor, while SCP-XXXX-2 cries, his hands on his face.

They aren't 'seconds of silence' if -2 is crying; and this is implied to be an audio transcript (from the 'Audio recorded' in the foreword), so how do they know from the recording what the SCP was doing?

without my approbation

'approbation' isn't like, incorrect here but it feels…like an odd choice of words.

ShortSmall— silence.

Ideally you'd specify a duration here over saying 'short' but *shrugs*

Upon a demand made by SCP-XXXX-2 to Dr. Young

This feels really iffy because like…we don't actually learn what the demand is? Did -2 just demand to see Morter? It should explicitly say what it was imo.

[-] Line By Line

item.title: No man's an island
item.content:encoded:
http://scp-sandbox-3.wikidot.com/retrom

The story of a lonely SCP and the doctor who became his friend.

It's the first time I write on here, so actually pretty much any advice or critique would help me improve it so I can post it eventually, but I would really like help about the formatting of the page, the structure of my story elements and dialogue tips as well.

The title came from Grigori Karpin as I have really no other idea for a title, so if someone has something else, it could be nice.

Also, here's the link to my greenlight : http://www.scpwiki.com/forum/t-13816271 and it is in my sandbox as well.

The article is 2,245 words long and it's important to note that there is a bit of violence (self-harm) in the incident report addendum.

Hope you (the kind reviewer who sees this) like it and merry christmas in advance.
